CHIEF COMPLAINT
Incidentally discovered right upper lobe lung nodule found on chest imaging.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a cyclist with a three-month history of intermittent cough that began after loading hay bales while caring for horses. Patient subsequently developed a cold and presented to primary care physician. Chest X-ray obtained to rule out pneumonia revealed a lung nodule. Subsequent CT scan confirmed the nodule. Patient denies current cough, pain, or shortness of breath. Patient reports feeling better overall and states cough has resolved.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies current cough, pain, or shortness of breath. Reports history of intermittent cough for approximately three months, now resolved.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Rheumatoid arthritis - currently fair control
2. Previous smoker - quit approximately 7 years ago

MEDICATIONS
1. Methotrexate 7.5 mg weekly for rheumatoid arthritis

ALLERGIES
Not documented in this visit.

FAMILY HISTORY
Mother with history of breast cancer, currently doing well. No family history of lung cancer or other malignancies. No personal or family history of lung infections or pneumonia.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is an active cyclist who frequently bikes on local trails. Previously smoked but quit approximately 7 years ago and has remained tobacco-free. Owns horses and performs farm work including hay baling. Lives with children who supported smoking cessation efforts.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: BP 124/76, HR 70, RR 16, O2 sat 98% on room air, afebrile
Lungs: Clear and equal bilateral on auscultation
Heart: Regular rate and rhythm, no clicks, rubs, or murmurs, no extra beats
Extremities: Pink, warm, and dry skin. No edema to lower extremities. Mild swelling of knuckles on third digits bilaterally consistent with rheumatoid arthritis. Pulses intact in all extremities with brisk capillary refill.

RESULTS
Chest CT: Solitary 2 cm smooth nodule in lateral aspect of right upper lobe. No evidence of emphysematous disease.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Right upper lobe lung nodule - Order pulmonary function tests for baseline lung function assessment. Schedule PET CT to determine if nodule is metabolically active. Plan video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) with three small incisions to right chest for nodule removal and biopsy. Procedure under general anesthesia, approximately 1.5 hours duration. Admit post-procedure with chest tube expected to remain until following day. Hospital stay anticipated to be one night. Removal recommended given smoking history despite possibility of benign etiology.

2. Rheumatoid arthritis - Continue current management with rheumatologist. Continue methotrexate therapy as previously outlined.

Patient counseled regarding diagnosis and treatment plan. Patient expresses anxiety regarding procedure but agrees to proceed. Reassured of physician support throughout treatment process.
